POV: “I’ll eat healthy tomorrow” starts right after this bite 😭  Creamy Cheesy Buldak Noodles 🌶️🧀 Ingredients 2 slices American cheese 1 slice baby Swiss cheese 2 tbsp ketchup 2 tbsp Kewpie mayo 1 tbsp chili oil (plus more for topping) 1 packet Buldak sauce and seasoning powder 2–3 tbsp chopped green onions (plus more for garnish) ½ cup heavy cream 1 packet Buldak noodles, boiled until half cooked Cooked dumplings, for topping Cooked sausage, sliced, for topping Instructions In a pan over low heat, add the American cheese and baby Swiss cheese. Add the ketchup, Kewpie mayo, chili oil, Buldak sauce, seasoning powder, and chopped green onions. Stir until the cheese melts and everything is well combined. Pour in the heavy cream and mix until the sauce is smooth and creamy. Add the half-cooked Buldak noodles and toss until every strand is coated in the rich, cheesy sauce. Top with cooked dumplings and sliced sausage. Finish with an extra drizzle of chili oil and more chopped green onions. Serve hot and enjoy! #r#ramenb#buldakr#Recipec#cookspicy

Most businesses do not die from lack of passion, my friend. They die because the founder never learned five numbers. ROI — if you spent one hundred dollars, how much comes back? No clear answer, no investment. Cashflow — if cash is not moving, the business is not breathing. CAC and LTV — what a customer costs you, against what he pays you over time. If the first is bigger, you are quietly bleeding. Break-even — the number of sales that covers everything. Know it, or you are guessing. The cost of your time — forty hours for two hundred dollars is not a business. It is a prison with your name on the lease. Passion makes the work bearable. Numbers make it profitable. Creamy Cheesy Buldak Ramen 🍜🧀🔥 Ingredients 1 pack Buldak ramen 1 slice baby Swiss cheese 1 slice American cheese 1 slice Monterey Jack cheese 2 tbsp mayo Buldak sauce packet Buldak powder packet Chili oil 2 cloves garlic, minced 2 tbsp chopped green onions ½ cup heavy cream or milk Cooked ramen noodles Toppings Fried egg Mini sausages Dumplings Extra green onions Extra chili oil Instructions Cook the Buldak noodles according to package instructions. Drain and set aside. In a pan over low heat, add the baby Swiss, American, and Monterey Jack cheese slices. Add the mayo, Buldak sauce, Buldak powder, chili oil, minced garlic, and green onions on top of the cheese. Mix everything together until the cheese melts into a thick spicy paste. Pour in the heavy cream or milk and stir until smooth and creamy. Add the cooked noodles and toss until fully coated in the sauce. Top with fried egg, dumplings, mini sausages, extra green onions, and more chili oil if desired. Enjoy hot and creamy  #buldak #buldakramen #eat #food  #Foodie

Skincare Ingredients — AM☀️ vs PM🌙 Wondering if you're using your skincare at the right time? Here's a pharmacist’s guide to AM vs PM skincare timing ⏰ ☀️ Vitamin C - AM > PM → Pairs with SPF to fight free radical damage from UV exposure ☀️ Niacinamide - AM > PM → Flexible ingredient, but in the morning it calms skin and balances oil before sunscreen and makeup 🔄 Hyaluronic Acid - AM & PM → Works 24/7. Must apply on damp skin to lock in deep hydration 🔄 Ceramides - AM & PM → Essential for barrier repair, especially after using retinoids or acids 🌙 Retinol - PM only → It breaks down in sunlight and increases sun sensitivity 🌙 Salicylic Acid - AM < PM → Works either time, but preferred at night to deep-clean pores while the skin regenerates overnight 🌙 Lactic Acid - PM only → Gentle AHA that exfoliates surface cells but increases sun sensitivity  Save this for your next skincare routine — and follow for Part 2 ✨ #skintok #niacinamide #retinol #skincareroutine #hyaluronicacid

“Dog lovers” vs dog lovers when it comes to greeting dogs! ETA: “dog lovers” could also be replaced with “uniformed, uneducated, and/or inconsiderate dog lovers” vs “informed, educated, and considerate dog lovers” if that makes you more comfortable 🫶 One of my biggest pet peeves is people baby talking to my dog and pretending like I’m interrupting? Bizarre! And in case you didn’t know because it’s something that’s been so normalized, putting your hands in dogs’ faces is unsafe. Dogs don’t need to sniff you up close like that and it’s putting unneeded pressure on them (often leading to bites). The best way to greet a dog is calm, neutral, and honestly just ignoring them. If you want to say hi to a dog, ask the owner first. Try to make yourself small by turning to the side and crouching. Allow the dog to approach you first. Some dogs are super friendly and love people! This doesn’t mean it’s ok to pet or approach without asking their handler! The safest way to greet any dog is by admiring from afar. Admittedly, if I know someone’s dog well, I might be a bit of the former “dog lover” and be excitedly greeting them 😂 It’s different when you know the dog!
